jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Smart Money
jokes.joke: I get very judgmental in casinos. I watched a guy lose three hundred dollars at blackjack and thought, “How do you just ignore the numbers like that?” Then I went to the ATM. Twelve-dollar fee to withdraw forty bucks. I stared at that screen, shook my head, and said, “Hit me.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Open Late
jokes.joke: I own a small business, so I know what a casino feels like from the inside. Every month I put everything I have on the table, the house always wins, and I’m told it’s called ‘taxes.’ The difference is the casino gives me free drinks. My accountant just gives me a bill and a look that says, ‘You know you could have walked away.’

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Retail Profiling
jokes.joke: I run a small business, which is just a polite way of saying I am professionally judgmental. You can’t survive retail without profiling people instantly. If a guy walks into my shop wearing a fedora and spotless cargo shorts, I already know two things: he’s going to ask fourteen highly specific questions about a twelve-dollar item, and he is absolutely not going to buy it.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: House Odds
jokes.joke: I’m a small business owner. Every day I’m gambling on inventory, on customers showing up, on the rent not going up. So the first time I walked into a casino it felt familiar. I sat at the table and told the dealer, “Just give me the house odds—I’m used to them.” He dealt. I lost. And for once, nobody followed up with a survey asking how they could improve my experience.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: House Edge
jokes.joke: I'm a small business owner, so I tried a casino hoping to finally be on the profitable side of math. After three hours I realized it's exactly like running my shop: strangers wander around, nobody reads the signs, and somehow all the money disappears. The only difference is the casino sends someone over when I'm losing too fast and asks if I'd like a free drink.
